not_published.why: Not announced as of 2026-10-21. No 2027 Part B notice in the Federal Register (FR API search, newest is 2025-20251 for 2026) and ssa.gov/cola says 2027 Medicare information 'will be available' later. CMS historically announces in Oct-Nov.

The 3.6% COLA and 2027 earnings-test amounts are on ssa.gov, but the Federal Register 'Cost-of-Living Increase and Other Determinations for 2027' notice is not yet published.
ADOR has not published 2026 forms; statute's indexing language is ambiguous (see flags).

Form SSA-44 itself not read (www.ssa.gov blocks scripted fetches); the controlling list is 20 CFR 418.1205, recorded instead.

flags: IRMAA boundaries are not uniform: tiers 1-3 upper bounds are inclusive ('less than or equal to'), tier 4 upper bound is exclusive ('less than $500,000'), top tier is 'greater than or equal to'. Code must use > and <= for tiers 1-3, and >= for $500k/$750k.

20 CFR 418.1105(c) says CMS will index 'all modified adjusted gross income threshold amounts', but the statute (§1839(i)(5)(C)) freezes the $500,000 (and so $750,000) amounts until 2028, indexed then from an August 2026 base. The regulation text is outdated; follow the statute (CMS's FR notice agrees).
MFS (lived with spouse) IRMAA upper band changed $394,000 (2025) -> $391,000 (2026): it is $500,000 minus the single threshold, so it falls as the single threshold rises. Do not hard-code.
IRMAA MAGI and ACA MAGI differ: ACA adds nontaxable Social Security (§36B(d)(2)(B)(iii)); IRMAA does not (20 CFR 418.1010(b)(6)).

RMD birth-year-1959: statute gives both 73 and 75. Final regs (T.D. 10001) reserve §1.401(a)(9)-2(b)(2)(v); proposed REG-103529-23 says 73. Not finalized as of 2026-10-20 (FR search). Proposed regs are not binding but signal IRS position; a technical correction in legislation has not been verified.
Uniform Lifetime Table in the regulation starts at age 72, not 70 or 73.

Inherited IRA annual RMDs (owner died on/after RBD) required starting 2025; 2021-2024 waived by Notices 2022-53, 2023-54, 2024-35. I found no 2025 or later notice extending relief (searched FR only; did not exhaustively search IRS bulletins).

Arizona: The 2025 senior subtraction was first offered administratively (EO 2025-15, 2025-11-25, and ADOR's 2025 forms/MCTCP worksheet) before any law; it became law only on 2026-06-13 (HB 4168, Laws 2026 ch. 140, retroactive to tax years after 2024). SB 1106 (vetoed 2026-01-16) and HB 2785 (vetoed 2026-02-12) did NOT become law.

Arizona: A.R.S. §43-1041 sets $15,750/$23,625/$31,500 'subject to subsection H', which indexes 'from and after December 31, 2019'. Literal reading could compound indexing on top of 2025 dollars; intended reading is probably to track the federal basic standard deduction (2026: $16,100/$24,150/$32,200). Confirm with ADOR's 2026 Form 140 (expected ~Dec 2026).

Arizona: azleg shows two versions of §43-1011 (01011.htm: L21 Ch. 411, with graduated brackets plus surcharge cap; 01011.01.htm 'Version 1': L21 Ch. 412 with flat 2.5% in paragraph 9 after §43-243 triggers). ADOR's 2025 Form 140 applies the flat 2.5%. I relied on ADOR plus Version 1 and did not trace the §43-243 trigger notice.

Arizona age-65 exemption $2,100 (A.R.S. §43-1023(E)) is separate from and in addition to the $6,000 senior subtraction (§43-1022(35)). Arizona does not use the federal additional standard deduction for age 65.

ACA: enhanced credits expired after 2025. H.R. 1834 (3-year extension) passed the House 2026-01-08 but sits on the Senate calendar (no action after 2026-02-10). No extension enacted as of 2026-10-21 per congress.gov; absence of another law was checked by search, not by reading every 2026 public law.
ACA 2026 repayment: OBBBA §71305 removed the excess-APTC repayment caps for tax years beginning after 2025. 2025 caps still apply to 2025 returns.
ACA 2026 uses 2025 poverty guidelines ($15,650 / $21,150), not the 2026 ones ($15,960 / $21,640), because of the 'most recently published as of first day of open enrollment' rule.

Social Security 2027 COLA (3.6%) and 2027 earnings-test amounts come from ssa.gov only; the Federal Register notice is not out yet. ssa.gov pages block scripted fetches (HTTP 403); I read them in a browser.
FRA: worker and survivor FRA tables differ (survivor schedule lags by 2 birth years). Birthdays on Jan 1 belong to the prior birth year (attain age the day before the birthday).
IRMAA amounts recorded are full Part B coverage only; the immunosuppressive-drug-only Part B tables (different amounts) were left out.
